01 / climb

V9and still pushing.

Bouldering is the kind of climbing where you fall a lot. I’ve done it long enough to climb V9 — hard enough that each new grade costs months, easy enough that the next one still feels possible. That gap is where I like to live.

03 / build

Things I build.Mostly for fun. Sometimes for money.

By day I build and test AI products for pharmaceutical clients at The RxAssistant. Before that, R&D at a quant shop: earnings models, order books, strategies that survived contact with production. Computer science at the University of Delaware, class of 2027. Everything below happened at night.

  • 01

    Short-form video, end to end

    A Python pipeline that scrapes a script, voices it, subtitles it with whisper, cuts it with MoviePy and ffmpeg, and uploads it through the YouTube Data API while I sleep.

    python · whisper · ffmpeg
  • 02

    Order books, live

    Java on EC2 watching 200+ crypto markets through Kraken’s API around the clock, keeping the order-book history that nobody publishes.

    java · aws · kraken
  • 03

    Earnings → direction

    Fifteen model variants trained on reports, guidance, and analyst estimates. 57% next-day direction accuracy in backtests, which is a bigger number than it sounds.

    python · ml · backtesting
  • 04

    This website

    Hand-written HTML on a Jetson in my room, reached through an outbound-only Cloudflare tunnel, with a 9B-parameter model answering questions one section down. No framework. No cloud AI.

    caddy · llama.cpp · cloudflare tunnel

C · C++ · Python · Java · React · Linux · AWS · Postgres · and whatever the problem needs

04 / machine

Talk to the machine.It lives on my desk. It is serving you this page.

Most “AI on a website” is a request to somebody else’s datacenter. This is a nine-billion-parameter model running on the GPU of the Jetson under my desk — the same board that just sent you this HTML. When it answers, watch the power draw on the right climb.
